# Pinned JavaScript import reference

Upstream: `antlr/grammars-v4`, commit
`89fd36482e8cb68a4e55df021a8adbc7541b52f2`. `UPSTREAM.json` records exact
URLs and SHA-256 hashes for both grammars, the required Java base classes,
and upstream's compatibility notes. Sources are unmodified. `LICENSE` copies
the MIT notice from the grammar files; those original notices are retained.
The base classes are reference sources, not compiled or executed by W.

`BLOCKERS.txt` is the complete deterministic semantic audit for these two
pinned grammar inputs, regenerated by the command below. The normal strict
test compares it byte for byte and verifies all source hashes without network
access. The translator intentionally refuses to publish JavaScript output.

```sh
bin/antlr_to_pg --strict \
  libs/extras/grammars/antlr_to_pg/testdata/antlr/javascript/JavaScriptLexer.g4 \
  libs/extras/grammars/antlr_to_pg/testdata/antlr/javascript/JavaScriptParser.g4 \
  -o bin/javascript-import.pg \
  --audit bin/javascript-import.audit
```

`ADAPTATIONS.json` links every reported source site (file, offset, exact text,
rule and location) to the reviewed native files, or explicitly records it as
deferred. `adapted-subset` describes design correspondence, not complete
upstream equivalence. The compatibility runner verifies every expected source
anchor and hash before running cases; an upstream edit requires an explicit
ledger update. This profile does not paste foreign actions into W or silently
turn unknown actions into no-ops.

The native grammar uses parser-directed regex goals rather than the upstream
base class's previous-token heuristic. It uses checkpointed template/brace
state, explicit contextual keyword alternatives, pure newline predicates,
Unicode-aware matchers, and precedence tiers. Strict-mode keyword/string
behavior, Annex B HTML/CDATA comments, and the upstream ERROR channel require
separate compatibility review. These exclusions remain visible in the ledger.

The upstream README explicitly disclaims exact ECMAScript conformance. Its
current revision also includes features newer than ES2020, so a successful
import could not by itself establish the project's chosen edition baseline.
